system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. The separate medium_decision already settles medium authorization and taxonomy: copy its schema-owned medium, transform phrase/target and style constants exactly; do not reinterpret them. Return only the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the whole request semantically, without keyword lists.
With NO visual reference, every attribute is request-governed, transform_phrase/transform_target are empty (there is nothing to transfer from), and style follows the actual requested medium/treatments or the explicit default Live-action, cinematic. The visual reference governs every attribute that the user has not explicitly specified. The user's specified action overrides a subject plate's static pose. Introducing temporal motion into a still while preserving its depicted look is an action instruction, not by itself a request to change rendering medium. Requesting a wide target aspect or duration is canvas/timing configuration, not an instruction about camera framing/composition, lighting or visual medium. Explicit wardrobe, lighting, framing or palette instructions override the corresponding reference attribute only. A throwaway or descriptive style adjective (including a loose medium name) is NOT authorization to transform an attached reference. A clear request to restyle/reimagine/redraw/convert, including participles and irregular forms, or an explicit target rendering instruction authorizes a medium transformation. User supplied Brief.style is an explicit structured target style. Keep identity retention independent of rendering-medium transformation: do not choose attribute_transfer merely to change a medium.
Return transform_phrase as an exact quote of the user's transformation instruction, and transform_target as its complete target medium noun phrase; use empty strings if none. medium is request-governed only for a genuine transformation or explicit Brief.style. Do not cut off long target phrases. With a visual reference and no transformation, preserve its observed medium. Treatment words such as cinematic/moody may ride on top without replacing medium. A different style name in the same medium bucket is not a medium discrepancy. discrepancy is true only for an unapproved incompatible medium request versus reference; explain that the reference is retained and that an explicit reimagine/restyle instruction would change it. Unknown reference medium cannot establish a discrepancy.
Style phrase must be grammatical and concrete, with the winning medium and compatible requested treatments. Use actual observed Card styles, not stale Asset.Description. In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed medium and lighting before incoming identity plates; a replacement/placement image supplies identity only and must not replace the clip's world with portrait/studio photography. A reference sheet's studio lighting, panel arrangement, labels, views and posing are presentation; never make them the scene. Scene reference lighting may inform style unless the user owns lighting. Explicit requests outrank references; references outrank director notes. Director notes only fill unspecified space, never override a retained reference medium. Reference facts must not be invented. Existing pose is recorded separately and licensed only when that input is an actual frame anchor, never in subject identity or retention. reference_medium and requested_medium are classification IDs, never free-form style prose: use exactly empty-string for unknown, 2d-animation, 3d-animation, archival, stop-motion, painted, or live-action. observed_phrase records the full winning observed look; phrase records the target look. Independent reference_readings are real supplied visual readings even when no media is being attached in this analysis-only operation. Return reasoning for every attribute.
For each observed subject, descriptor preserves the exact observed identifier except that reference-sheet descriptors must remove view/panel qualifiers (eight views of one person are one identity). This descriptor must not describe the sheet layout, mood inference or pose. For each observed subject, identity retains every stable observed attribute unless that exact attribute conflicts with an explicit user change. retained_attributes must be exact original strings, never pose, interpretation, scene lighting, or panel/view labels. If a wardrobe change is requested, drop only the replaced wardrobe attributes and keep hair/scars/other unchanged identity. requested_attributes are only explicit target identity/wardrobe changes, with request_quote quoting their authorizing words exactly; they must not be invented by creativity or director. Keep requested_attributes empty and request_quote empty when no such change was requested. wardrobe_attributes is the subset of retained_attributes describing garments/accessories only; do not put hair, scars, pose, scene or camera properties there. Descriptor, subject kind and original sources remain host-owned. The source reading remains recorded separately; these are target definition permissions.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: A composite character reference sheet for one lean adult in all-black tactical clothing. A rainy nighttime hero shot sits above front, side-profile, and back studio views, followed by close-ups of the face, jacket collar, hands, and boots.

subjects.descriptor: The single character identity shown across all panels: a lean adult with short shaved sides and dark hair tied in a top knot, wearing all-black tactical clothing.
attributes: dark hair tied in a small top knot
visible small mark or scar above one eyebrow
black high-collared tactical jacket with chest straps and buckles
pose: Hero panel: standing upright, body toward the camera, head turned to the viewer’s left
Front panel: standing facing the camera, arms at the sides
Side profile: standing in profile facing left, arms relaxed at the sides
Back panel: standing facing away from the camera
Face detail: neutral expression, looking toward the camera
Hands detail: hands relaxed and open
Boots detail: feet planted

cards.environment: Top panel: rainy nighttime urban walkway or bridge between dark buildings, with metal railings and distant warm lights. Studio panels use a dark gray or black seamless backdrop.
cards.lighting: Top panel: cool cinematic night lighting with rain, strong reflections on wet pavement, and warm amber background bokeh. Studio panels: low-key soft directional lighting that reveals clothing texture and facial features.
cards.framing: Vertical composite layout: one large full-body environmental hero image at the top, three full-body studio views in the middle row, and four detail crops across the bottom row, with centered uppercase labels beneath them.
cards.style: Photorealistic cinematic character-design reference sheet or concept art, moody and low-key.
cards.characterisation: One tactical, wet-weather character identity presented through multiple reference views and detail studies.

cards.summary: Dark fantasy dragon creature reference sheet with one large atmospheric scene and seven smaller labeled views and close-up detail panels.

subjects.descriptor: single dark dragon design shown across multiple reference views and detail panels
attributes: spiked crest along the head, neck, and back
large membranous bat-like wings with visible finger supports
pose: large scene: side profile with head lowered and wings extended
FRONT panel: facing forward with wings spread
SIDE PROFILE panel: side view with wings partly extended
REAR panel: rear view with wings spread
HEAD CLOSE panel: close frontal/three-quarter head view
WING MEMBRANE panel: close view of the wing membrane
CLAW AND FOOT panel: close view of a forefoot and claws
SCALE DETAIL panel: close view of overlapping scales

cards.environment: Main scene: dark volcanic rocky landscape with wet reflective ground, mist, and small lava or ember glows. Smaller panels: dark neutral studio-like background.
cards.lighting: Low-key, moody lighting with cool blue-grey highlights in the main scene, warm orange lava/ember accents, and dark controlled lighting in the reference panels.
cards.framing: Composite reference sheet: a large top banner image above two rows of smaller panels.
cards.style: Dark fantasy creature design and concept-art reference sheet with highly detailed rendering.
cards.characterisation: The dragon is depicted as an imposing, heavily armored fantasy creature with large wings, prominent horns, and a spiked dorsal crest.

medium_decision.reasoning: The request describes an action scene with cinematic camera/expression direction, but it does not expressly ask to change or reimagine the reference's rendering medium. The loose term 'cinematic' is a treatment, not authorization for medium conversion.
